0001 - Documentation approach

docs.title: 0001 - Documentation approach
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-08 Code: ADR-0001

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Wishlist consists of separate repositories for the backend API and the web client. Product, architecture and feature knowledge spans both, so it needs a single home that is versioned, reviewable and always up to date. This documentation was created so each technical decision stays trackable.

docs.title: Central docs repository
docs.text: All cross-documentation lives in wishlist-docs. Code repositories keep only their own README and setup instructions, and link here.

docs.title: Docs as code
docs.text: Documentation is written in Markdown with Mermaid diagrams and versioned in git. Initially, changes are committed directly to the dev branch; pull requests will be introduced once more contributors join. Initial commit goes to main.

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text: MkDocs 1.x with the Material theme builds the site, and mike handles versioning. All tool versions are pinned in requirements.txt so builds stay reproducible.

docs.title: Document types
docs.text: We will use ASDs and ADRs, to answer the following questions: what? and why?.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
wishlist-docs/
├── mkdocs.yml              site configuration
├── requirements.txt        pinned tool versions
└── docs/
    ├── index.md            overview page
    ├── product/            vision, glossary
    ├── asd/                index, feature specs (NNN-name.md)
    ├── architecture/       index, auth, data model, i18n
    ├── adr/                index, decision records (NNNN-name.md)
    ├── operations/         environments, deployment, runbook
    └── contributing/       workflow, writing docs

docs.title: Continuous delivery with two versions
docs.text:
The branching model is a simplified Git Flow.

  • The main branch builds latest: the production docs and the default version of the site.
  • The dev branch builds dev: work in progress, published alongside latest with a banner marking it as the development version.
  • Every push to main or dev is built and deployed automatically by CI. Releases are made by merging dev into main.

docs.title: CI pipeline
docs.text:
The docs workflow runs on GitHub Actions and publishes both versions to GitHub Pages.

flowchart TD
    S1["<b>1:</b> Push to dev or main"] --> S2["<b>2:</b> Prepare build"]
    S2 --> S3{"<b>3:</b> Which branch?"}
    S3 -->|dev| S4a["<b>4a:</b> Deploy dev"]
    S3 -->|main| S4b["<b>4b:</b> Deploy latest"]
    S4a --> S5["<b>5:</b> GitHub Pages publishes"]
    S4b --> S5
# Step What happens Runs on 1 Push A push to dev or main starts the workflow. Other branches are ignored. dev, main 2 Prepare build A fresh runner checks out the repository and installs the pinned tools from requirements.txt. dev, main 3 Branch check The pushed branch decides which version is built. dev, main 4a Deploy dev mike builds the site into the dev/ folder of the gh-pages branch, with the development banner. dev 4b Deploy latest mike builds the site into the latest/ folder and makes it the default version. main 5 Publish GitHub Pages serves the gh-pages branch: the root URL opens latest, and /dev/ opens dev. dev, main

docs.title: GitHub wikis
docs.text: Wikis will be disabled in all Wishlist repositories so the docs site remains the single source of truth.

docs.title: Writing conventions (preparing for AI)
docs.text:
• No manual line breaks inside paragraphs or list items; each paragraph is a single line.
  • No numbered lists for sections; use ### headers instead.
  • No arrow characters (such as → or ->) in prose; describe the relationship in words. Arrows are allowed only inside Mermaid diagrams and code.
  • No em dashes; use a colon, comma, parentheses or a new sentence instead.
  • Tables are used only to explain flow diagrams and are placed directly below the diagram they describe. Everything else uses ### headers and bullet points.
  • Each diagram node is numbered in its label (e.g. 1: Push to dev or main), and the table has exactly one row per node, in the same order.
  • The first column (#) holds the step number in bold, matching the number in the diagram. Branching steps use letter suffixes (e.g. 8a, 8b).
  • The second column holds the step name in bold; the remaining columns hold plain-text detail.
  • Table cells contain a single line of text: no line breaks, no nested lists.
  • Diagram labels use a colon after the number (1:), not a period, because Mermaid can misread 1. as a Markdown list.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One place to look for product and architecture knowledge, with its full history in git.
  • Readers can always see both the released state (latest) and upcoming changes (dev).
  • Code commits that change behavior reference the related ASD in the commit message (e.g. ASD-002: hide reservations from list owner), and the matching docs change is committed to dev in the docs repository at the same time, or the docs will drift.
  • Once pull requests are introduced, feature PRs in the code repositories must link to the matching docs PR.
  • MkDocs 1.x is no longer maintained upstream and Material for MkDocs reaches end of life in November 2026. Pinned versions keep the build working in the meantime; migration to Zensical will be evaluated in ADR XXXX.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: How changes to the documentation are made, published and released.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
• main: the released documentation, published as latest. Only updated by merging dev.
  • dev: work in progress for the upcoming release, published as dev.

Pull requests are not used yet; changes are committed directly to dev.

docs.title: Making a change
docs.text:
• Switch to dev and pull the latest changes: git checkout dev && git pull.
  • Start the local preview with mkdocs serve and edit the files in docs/.
  • Commit with a message that follows the commit conventions below.
  • Push to dev. CI publishes the dev version automatically.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
• Feature work: start with the ASD code, e.g. ASD-001: add SSO flow.
  • Decisions: start with the ADR code, e.g. ADR-0002: evaluate Zensical.
  • Everything else: start with docs:, e.g. docs: fix typo in glossary.

Commits in the code repositories that change behavior reference the related ASD code the same way, and the matching docs change is committed to dev at the same time.

docs.title: Adding an ASD or ADR
docs.text:
Not supported

Don't modify already published ADRs.

  • Copy the template from docs/contributing/templates/ (asd.md or adr.md) into docs/asd/ or docs/adr/.
  • Give it the next free number: NNN-name.md for ASDs, NNNN-name.md for ADRs.
  • Fill in the header (title, date, code, status).
  • Add it to the section's index.md under today's date.
  • Add it to nav: in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
• Make sure dev contains everything for the release and builds without warnings.
  • Merge dev into main and push: git checkout main && git merge dev && git push.
  • Tag the release with the application version: git tag vX.Y.Z && git push --tags.
  • CI publishes the new latest version.

docs.title: Writing docs
docs.text: Conventions that keep the documentation consistent and easy to read for both people and AI tools.

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
• No manual line breaks inside paragraphs or list items; each paragraph is a single line.
  • No numbered lists for sections; use ### headers instead.
  • No arrow characters (such as → or ->) in prose; describe the relationship in words. Arrows are allowed only inside Mermaid diagrams and code.
  • No em dashes; use a colon, comma, parentheses or a new sentence instead.

docs.title: File names and codes
docs.text:
• ASDs: files are named NNN-name.md (e.g. 001-auth-sso.md), the code is ASD-NNN.
  • ADRs: files are named NNNN-name.md (e.g. 0001-documentation-approach.md), the code is ADR-NNNN.
  • Numbers are never reused or changed. The code appears in the page header and in commit messages.

docs.text:

docs.title: Diagrams and tables
docs.text:
• Tables are used only to explain flow diagrams and are placed directly below the diagram they describe. Everything else uses ### headers and bullet points.
  • Each diagram node is numbered in bold in its label (e.g. <b>1:</b> Push to dev or main), and the table has exactly one row per node, in the same order.
  • The first column (#) holds the step number in bold, matching the number in the diagram. Branching steps use letter suffixes (e.g. 4a, 4b).
  • The second column holds the step name in bold; the remaining columns hold plain-text detail.
  • Table cells contain a single line of text: no line breaks, no nested lists.
  • Diagram labels use a colon after the number (1:), not a period, because Mermaid can misread 1. as a Markdown list.

docs.title: Callouts
docs.text: Callouts (admonitions) highlight information that should stand out from the surrounding text. Each callout has a type, which sets its color and icon, and an optional title in quotes. The content must be indented by 4 spaces, or it renders outside the box.

docs.title: note
docs.text:
General remarks that are useful but not critical.

Note

The API reference is generated from the backend's OpenAPI file.

!!! note
    The API reference is generated from the backend's OpenAPI file.

docs.title: abstract
docs.text:
A short summary at the top of a long page. Aliases: summary, tldr.

Summary

Shared wishlists let invited users see items and reserve gifts without the owner knowing.

!!! abstract "Summary"
    Shared wishlists let invited users see items and reserve gifts without the owner knowing.

docs.title: info
docs.text:
Neutral background information or context.

Info

Sign-in currently supports Google and Apple accounts.

!!! info
    Sign-in currently supports Google and Apple accounts.

docs.title: todo
docs.text:
Marks a page or section that is not finalized. Alias of info.

Not finalized

This page is a draft and may change.

!!! todo "Not finalized"
    This page is a draft and may change.

docs.title: tip
docs.text:
Advice that makes something easier. Aliases: hint, important.

Tip

Run mkdocs serve while writing to see changes live.

!!! tip
    Run `mkdocs serve` while writing to see changes live.

docs.title: success
docs.text:
Something that is done, confirmed or working. Aliases: check, done.

Done

Google sign-in is implemented and deployed.

!!! success "Done"
    Google sign-in is implemented and deployed.

docs.title: question
docs.text:
An open question that still needs an answer. Aliases: help, faq.

Open question

Should reservations expire after the event date?

!!! question "Open question"
    Should reservations expire after the event date?

docs.title: warning
docs.text:
Something the reader must be careful about. Aliases: caution, attention.

Warning

Changing the database schema requires a new Drizzle migration.

!!! warning
    Changing the database schema requires a new Drizzle migration.

docs.title: failure
docs.text:
Something that does not work or is not supported. Aliases: fail, missing.

Not supported

LinkedIn sign-in is not available yet.

!!! failure "Not supported"
    LinkedIn sign-in is not available yet.

docs.title: danger
docs.text:
A risk of data loss, security issues or breaking production. Alias: error.

Danger

Never run seed scripts against the production database.

!!! danger
    Never run seed scripts against the production database.

docs.title: bug
docs.text:
A known issue and its workaround.

Known issue

The share link is not refreshed after renaming a wishlist. Reload the page as a workaround.

!!! bug "Known issue"
    The share link is not refreshed after renaming a wishlist. Reload the page as a workaround.

docs.title: example
docs.text:
A concrete example of a rule or concept.

Example

ASD-002: hide reservations from list owner is a correctly formatted commit message.

!!! example
    `ASD-002: hide reservations from list owner` is a correctly formatted commit message.

docs.title: quote
docs.text:
A quotation from a person, a document or an external source. Alias: cite.

Quote

Docs that drift from the code stop being read.

!!! quote
    Docs that drift from the code stop being read.

docs.title: Collapsible, closed by default
docs.text:
Use ??? instead of !!!. Good for long details most readers can skip. Requires pymdownx.details in mkdocs.yml.

Full error log

The complete output is kept here so it does not clutter the page.

??? info "Full error log"
    The complete output is kept here so it does not clutter the page.

docs.title: Collapsible, open by default
docs.text:
Use ???+.

Shortcut

Press / to jump to the search box.

???+ tip "Shortcut"
    Press `/` to jump to the search box.

docs.title: Without a title
docs.text:
Use an empty title to show only the content.

A callout without a title bar.

!!! note ""
    A callout without a title bar.

docs.title: When to use which callout
docs.text:
• todo: at the top of every unfinished page; remove it when the page is complete.
  • abstract: a one or two sentence summary at the top of long ASDs and ADRs.
  • question: open questions in ASDs, one callout per question.
  • warning: steps that can go wrong if done carelessly.
  • danger: anything that can lose data, leak secrets or break production.
  • bug: known issues in the runbook, each with its workaround.
  • success: confirmed, completed states, such as a feature that is implemented and deployed.
  • example: concrete examples next to a rule or convention.
  • Do not stack more than two callouts in a row; if everything stands out, nothing does.

docs.title: ADR (Architecture Decision Record)
docs.text: A short, append-only record of why a significant technical decision was made: its context, the decision and its consequences. A changed decision gets a new ADR that supersedes the old one. Stored in adr/ as NNNN-name.md.

docs.title: ASD (Application Specification Document)
docs.text: A living document that describes what a single feature should do: the problem, user stories, acceptance criteria and flows. Changes through pull requests. Stored in asd/ as ASD-NNN-name.md.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text: Testable conditions a feature must meet to be considered done, written as Given / When / Then.

docs.title: latest
docs.text: The production version of the docs, built from the main branch. The default version of the site.

docs.title: dev
docs.text: The work-in-progress version of the docs, built from the dev branch.

docs.title: mike
docs.text: The tool that publishes multiple versions (latest, dev) of the MKDocs docs side by side.
